correctness.rationale: For every prime-power \(q\), a fixed rank-one idempotent P yields \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&1-a\end{pmatrix}\) with \(a(1-a)=bc\), and target \(C=\begin{pmatrix}0&b\\-c&0\end{pmatrix}\). This bijection reduces the fiber count to \(\rho_q(\det C)\) times compatible ordered decompositions \(k^2=L\oplus M\). Their counts are \(q(q+1)\) for C=0, \(2q\) for nonzero nilpotent C, \(q+1-e(C)\) for nonscalar invertible traceless C, and zero for other cases. The scalar equation has quadratic-character or Artin--Schreier trace root counts. An independently proved character sum counts the odd-characteristic image, and a determinant-stratum count gives the even image. Actual package checker enumerated every pair and target over fields of orders 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11 including three extension fields; logged outputs matched. No finite enumeration is used as a proof of the unrestricted theorem.

value.rationale: Exact preimage cardinalities are a natural invariant of a restricted matrix word map, sharpening classical existence and determinant results. The theorem classifies every target across all finite fields, exposes the exact eigenline dependence and the characteristic-two trace obstruction, and computes the global image size including the odd \(q\bmod 4\) correction. Unlike a single arbitrary finite slice, this has an infinite-parameter structural interpretation.
